title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is ms. p. 767 of the continuation of La Longue Marche, §4°, 'L'isomorphisme GL(2,Z)~ ≃ ST_{1,1}'. On the previous page Grothendieck sets up the following. X_1 = R^2/Z^2 is the standard torus and U_{1,1} = X_1 − {0}. GL(2,Z) = Aut(X_1 as a topological group) fixes 0, which gives (37) GL(2,Z) → T_{1,1}, the isotopy classes of homeomorphisms of U_{1,1}, known to be an isomorphism. G = GL(2,Z) acts differentiably, and its tangent action at 0 is the tautological action on R^2. This yields an extension E of G by T_0 = Z: pull back the 'universal-cover' extension GL(2,R)~ of GL(2,R) along GL(2,Z) ⊂ GL(2,R). GL(2,R)~ is the group of homotopy classes of paths from 1, extended to the non-connected group, with orientation-reversing elements acting on π_1(GL^+) = Z by inversion. Equivalently, E is the action on oriented tangent directions at the fixed point, lifted to the universal cover of the circle of directions.

This page: (4°) E is canonically isomorphic, as an extension of G by Z, to the group GL(2,Z)~ defined in 3°. The parenthetical note says this works because R^2 and its quotient X_1 are canonically oriented. Hence the Theorem: pulling back along (37) the extension ST_{1,1} of T_{1,1} by Z gives canonically GL(2,Z)~. Here ST_{1,1} is the 'special' Teichmüller group: mapping classes of the surface with a tangent direction / boundary circle at the puncture, and the kernel Z is generated by the twist around the puncture. Consequently ST_{1,1} has the two explicit presentations of 3°.
(a) ρ̃^3 σ̃^{-2} = 1, i.e. ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2. This presents SL(2,Z)~ ≅ B_3 = π_1 of the trefoil complement. It is extended by an involution τ̃' acting by ρ̃ ↦ ρ̃^{-1}, σ̃ ↦ σ̃^{-1}, with τ̃'^2 = 1.
(b) Three involutions Γ̃_0, Γ̃_1, Γ̃_∞ with the single relation (Γ̃_0Γ̃_1)^3 (Γ̃_∞Γ̃_0)^2 = 1. This is consistent with (a) for ρ̃ = Γ̃_0Γ̃_1 and σ̃ = Γ̃_0Γ̃_∞. It lifts the Coxeter presentation of PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) reflection triangle group, in which (r_0r_1)^3 = 1 and (r_∞r_0)^2 = 1. In the Z-extension the lifts of the reflections stay involutions, and the two separate relations merge into the one relation (Γ̃_0Γ̃_1)^3 = (Γ̃_0Γ̃_∞)^2.

Grothendieck then announces a translation into fundamental groups. Choose a base point a_{1,1} in U_{1,1}, 'judiciously?'. Set (38) Π_{1,1} = π_1(U_{1,1}, a_{1,1}), free on x, y. Then (39) T_{1,1} ≅ Autext_loc(Π_{1,1}): outer automorphisms preserving the peripheral ('lacet') conjugacy class up to inversion, i.e. Dehn–Nielsen–Baer for the punctured torus. The next page gives ST_{1,1} as the normaliser of the loop subgroup L = ⟨l_0'⟩ in Aut_loc. It also plans to compute the action of the generators on x, y via the Z^2-cover R^2 − Z^2.

Purpose: an explicit, canonical, 'discrete' description of the genus-1 level of the Teichmüller tower (T_{1,1} and its Z-extension). The aim is to write down the action on π_1, presumably for use with the profinite/Galois action (Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme).
errors: The relation in (b), (Γ̃_0Γ̃_1)^3 · (Γ̃_∞Γ̃_0)^2 = 1, is correct only with the convention σ̃ = Γ̃_0Γ̃_∞, so that Γ̃_∞Γ̃_0 = σ̃^{-1}. Since ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 is central and conjugation by each Γ̃ inverts it, the relation is consistent. Signs and conventions are not stated on this page; they depend on 3°.
Minor grammar: 'donc il admet' should be 'elle admet' (referring to l'extension).

Grothendieck's own '(judicieusement ?)' flags that the choice of base point (at the puncture/tangential versus interior) was still unsettled. That choice matters for passing from Autext to Aut, as in (41) on the next page.

ideas.what: Mapping class group of the once-punctured torus ≅ GL(2,Z) via the linear action on R^2/Z^2 fixing 0.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions T_{1,1} and the genus-1 level of the Teichmüller tower; the explicit statement there is uncertain.

ideas.what: The Z-extension ST_{1,1} (twist around the puncture / tangent framing) identified with the pullback of the universal-cover extension of GL(2,R) via the tangent action at the fixed point.
ideas.modern_name: Mod(Σ_1^1) ≅ SL(2,Z)~ ≅ B_3 ⊂ SL(2,R)~ (plus orientation-reversing extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman–Hilden-type results; B_3 as preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R), e.g. Milnor)

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z)~ = B_3 ⋊ Z/2 by three involutions with the single relation (Γ_0Γ_1)^3 = (Γ_0Γ_∞)^2.
ideas.modern_name: Extended braid group B_3 ⋊ Z/2 (inversion automorphism) as a 'Coxeter-type' lift of the (2,3,∞) triangle reflection group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / easy consequence of aba = bab with τ inverting generators

ideas.what: T_{1,1} ≅ Autext_loc(π_1(U_{1,1})), and ST_{1,1} ≅ the normaliser of the peripheral loop subgroup in Aut_loc.
ideas.modern_name: Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem for punctured surfaces; Aut(F_2) stabiliser of [x,y]^{±1}
ideas.where_published: The 'Autext_loc' formalism appears in La Longue Marche (1981).

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, canonical identification of the genus-1 boundary/framed mapping class group with GL(2,Z)~ via the tangent action. It comes with a pleasant presentation by three involutions. All of this is classical or folklore (B_3 ≅ SL(2,Z)~, Dehn–Nielsen–Baer); the only mildly distinctive features are the systematic treatment with orientation-reversing elements and the involution presentation.
transcription_corrections: 'X̄_1' is probably just X_1, the torus quotient of R^2; the bar is likely a stroke.
'{+cf. tran. p. 761+}' probably reads 'cf. trav. p. 761' or similar, a cross-reference inserted to replace the struck-out 'la théorie'.
'S[-φ-]T_{1,1}': a struck letter before T, read as S𝒯_{1,1}.
In (b) the relation is written '(Γ̃_0Γ̃_1)^3 · (Γ̃_∞Γ̃_0)^2 = 1'; a struck-out annotation (possibly involving Γ̃_0) follows it.
In (a), 'τ̃'(ρ̃)' denotes the action (conjugation) of τ̃' on ρ̃.
